features.text: The patient is 49 years old and female.
The patient has chronic osteoarthritis in her elbows.
The patient's osteoarthritis has been flaring up lately.
The patient's elbow pain is described as a dull ache with occasional sharp pain.
The patient experiences swelling in her elbows, with the right elbow more swollen than the left.
The patient experiences stiffness in her elbows, especially in the morning or after sitting at her desk.
The patient has not had any previous injuries to her elbows.
The patient has been managing osteoarthritis with medication and work habit adjustments.
The patient is currently taking meloxicam 15 milligrams once a day for elbow pain and swelling.
The patient reports that meloxicam has helped with pain but not fully resolved swelling and stiffness.
The patient's elbow pain and stiffness have worsened over the past few weeks.
The patient has been sitting at her desk more, which she believes is contributing to the flare-up.
The patient has not had any imaging studies (X-rays or MRIs) for her elbows yet.
The patient was told by a doctor that an X-ray was ordered but has not had it done or seen the results.
The patient has not had any recent blood tests for inflammatory markers or autoimmune conditions.
The patient was told earlier that some labs (autoimmune panel, ESR, uric acid) were reviewed and everything looked good.
The patient occasionally feels numbness in her hands when typing for long periods, which resolves with shaking.
The patient has not experienced systemic symptoms such as fatigue, fever, weight loss, or rash in the past few months.
